script.text: One country's stock market lost five percent in a day. A Chinese chip plan may be why.

South Korea's Kospi index closed down 5.5 percent on Tuesday at 6,035, after falling more than 7 percent during the session, according to KED Global. SK Hynix fell about 10 percent. Samsung Electronics lost 7.4 percent, SBS reports.

Why? Chinese memory maker CXMT says it plans a new memory chip by year-end. Memory chips store data in phones and servers. Investors fear cheaper rivals. The claim is not independently verified. Samsung and SK Hynix make up about half the Kospi, an eToro analyst says, so their fall drags the whole index.
SBS reports foreign investors sold about 4.5 trillion won of Korean shares that day. It had already dropped 3.65 percent on Monday, to 6,384.
Will China's chip plan hold up under scrutiny? Yes or no?
